first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A Portugal wedding guide from a planning company: pick a region, here are the legal steps for my passport, then talk to one of their advisors. No packages and no price, so it's a guide that funnels to an enquiry form.

attention_map.quote: Get Married in Portugal, from a Sintra Palace to an Algarve Cliff
attention_map.why: Plain headline, no 'most exciting place in Europe' fluff. The quick answer on legal timing ('at least one month before the date') is a real number with a government source, so I keep going. 'one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend' is a promise I'll be checking against the rest of the page.

Season and guest count dropdowns straight under the headline before I know who you are or what you charge. 'Check your date' sounds like an availability check, but it is really just the enquiry form. Feels like a lead grab.

attention_map.quote: a non-numeric line naming Wedded Concierge and one Wedded Advisor, or hide the strip
attention_map.why: The proof strip either disappears or turns into a line that just repeats your own brand name. That isn't proof. If the numbers can't go up, there's nothing here telling me you've done this before.

attention_map.quote: Fall for Portugal Before You Choose a Venue
attention_map.why: Travel brochure stuff: Pena, Douro, sea stacks. Fine, but every one of my other tabs has it too. I did notice 'do not promise an unobstructed palace backdrop' for Monserrate, which is honest.

attention_map.quote: Setting; Best months; Nearest airport (code); Guests
attention_map.why: Same labelled lines on every card, so I can compare like for like. Then the Guests line is left blank or says 'Ask your Wedded Advisor' on every card. And the Comporta card gives an airport but no drive time when the others imply distances. That gap stands out when you're putting the cards side by side.

attention_map.quote: events on those dates may have to be cancelled
attention_map.why: This is the catch, said plainly, before I had to go digging. State events can bump a Queluz or Sintra palace booking, and Monserrate has scaffolding until Q1 2027. That's the kind of thing a salesy site leaves out. Big tick.

attention_map.quote: Exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms; a buy-out is often separate from the venue fee
attention_map.why: Exactly the hidden costs I'm hunting for. Telling me to check whether quotes include VAT is useful. It's about venue costs though, not your costs.

attention_map.quote: Fallback until then: explain what drives cost (guest count, region, season, nights at the venue, exclusivity) with no figures, and offer a Wedded Advisor estimate.
attention_map.why: If sign-off doesn't come through, the Costs tab has no numbers at all and just says ask an advisor. That's the classic 'call us for pricing' move. Even with the EUR 25,000 to 70,000 range, it's someone else's market figure for 100 guests, not your price, and there's nothing for smaller weddings.

attention_map.quote: Legal and cost details checked October 2026, with sources named in each tab.
attention_map.why: Separate AU, US and UK rules, official sources and a checked date. It's the most solid part of the page and better than the listicles I have open.

This is framed as what a weekend 'can include', not what you include. Who is the coordinator? The hero says one Wedded Advisor all the way through, and now there's a separate on-the-day person. Is that you, the venue, or something extra I pay for?
Free guest website. My first thought is what costs money after 'free'.

attention_map.quote: otherwise say a Wedded Advisor explains fees in your currency on the first call
attention_map.why: This is the part I care about most and it's the thinnest. Fees only on a call. 'Why book through you and not the venue' is answered from 'approved service facts only', and the brief doesn't say what those facts are. 'Wedded Privileges Tier 1' with no hotel names means nothing to me.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Four celebrity links in a section where your own real weddings are hidden. It looks like borrowing someone else's glamour because you can't show your own.

questions_answered.question: What is NOT included in the from price?
questions_answered.evidence: There is no from price and no list of what's included in the planning service. 'No Wedded Wonderland figure and no 'From AUD' price on this page.' s6 is 'what a weekend can include, not a package inclusion list'. The venue charges box covers venue extras (unoccupied rooms, buy-out, VAT), not your fee. Your own fee: 'a Wedded Advisor explains fees in your currency on the first call'.

questions_answered.question: Are these facts consistent across the page?
questions_answered.evidence: The brief promises 'one source of truth per fact id; same wording in tabs, cards and FAQ', and the legal, beach-permit and palace lines repeat cleanly. Weak spots: 'one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend' against 'an on-the-day coordinator'; guest count asked in the qualifier and form but blank on every region card; the Costs tab may show ranges or nothing depending on sign-off.

questions_answered.question: What proof is there that this team has done this venue before?
questions_answered.evidence: B8 numbers 'UNCONFIRMED' with a fallback of no numbers or a hidden strip; 'See Real Weddings in Portugal (HIDDEN AT LAUNCH): only 2 Portugal real weddings'; founder quote removed. No named venue the team has worked at. The only named weddings are celebrities.

questions_answered.question: Why book through you and not the venue directly?
questions_answered.evidence: s10 has the question but 'Answer from approved service facts only', with no content given. The only real reasons visible are one advisor as a single point of contact and the legal-by-passport help. Wedded Privileges has no Portugal hotels named.

questions_answered.question: What happens if something goes wrong on the day?
questions_answered.evidence: Only 'an on-the-day coordinator' in a list of what a weekend 'can include'. The brief's own open questions admit there's no approved line on this. The palace state-event cancellation is explained, but nothing about what you do if it happens to me.

objections_triggered.triggered_by: Proof strip hidden or replaced by a non-numeric brand line; real weddings hidden; celebrity trending row standing in for your own work

objections_triggered.objection: From price with no inclusions list means hidden costs
objections_triggered.triggered_by: No price for your service at all; fees 'explained on the first call'; Costs tab may fall back to 'no figures' plus 'a Wedded Advisor estimate'

objections_triggered.objection: Inconsistent numbers (capacity or rooms differ in two places)
objections_triggered.triggered_by: One advisor all the way through vs a separate on-the-day coordinator; guest count asked everywhere but given nowhere. Not numbers clashing yet, but the gaps make me suspicious

trust_signals_noticed: Palace catch stated up front: state events can cancel Queluz and National Palace of Sintra dates; Monserrate scaffolding to Q1 2027
Venue charges box: unoccupied rooms, separate buy-out, per-guest minimums, check whether VAT is included
'Legal and cost details checked October 2026, with sources named in each tab'
Legal rules split by Australian, US and UK passport with government sources linked
Honest that there's no package: 'no package, a planned weekend instead'
Same labelled lines on every region card so I can compare
turn_offs_noticed: Celebrity wedding links (Ronaldo, Perrie Edwards) while your own real weddings are hidden
'Check your date' qualifier straight under the headline, which is really a lead form
'Start for free' guest website: what's the catch after free?
'Wedded Privileges Tier 1' jargon with no Portugal hotels named

emotional_response.overall: Grudging respect for the honesty about palaces and venue charges, then deflated when I get to the part about you and find no proof and no fee.
emotional_response.trust: medium on the destination information, low on the company

payload.decision_reason: The page tells me more about the catches in Portugal than my other tabs do, so I'd bookmark it and use it as a checklist when I grill other planners. But I set myself a rule: no enquiry while a cost question is unanswered. Here your fee is only explained 'on the first call', there's nothing showing you've done a wedding in Portugal before, and nothing about what happens if the day goes wrong. Enquiring now means walking into a sales call blind.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Okay, credit where it's due: you told me a palace can cancel on me for a state event and that exclusivity can mean paying for empty rooms. Nobody else did. But what's the catch with you? No price, fees 'on the first call', proof strip hidden, real weddings hidden, and the only weddings you link to are Ronaldo's. You want me to pick a season and guest count before you've told me what you charge. I'm comparing three planners this week. The ones that show me a fee and a real Portugal wedding they ran will get my email first.
